text:
nina: heads up — nightly perf dashboard just flagged a ~20% p95 latency increase on canary starting ~01:10 UTC. throughput down ~12%. :eyes:
aj: saw that, looks correlated with a rise in kernel-switch events and an uptick in KV eviction rate on the same hosts.
marco: linking the graph: https://dash.redwood.local/d/rt/perf?from=01:00&to=02:00 — kernel_switch_rate spikes at 01:12, batching_window median jumps from ~10ms to ~36ms
meera: timeline: 01:05 CI merge of `platform/runtime:batch-scheduler-refactor` landed to canary pool. CI perf job didn't catch it (small test workload).
perf-bot: nightly-ci-run-5381234500 finished, p95_latency: baseline 78ms -> 94ms (+20%). unit-tests: ok.
aj: quick check of commits — PR #4029 changed default `batching.max_hold_ms` from 12 -> 40 and added a new warmup path in scheduler. suspect interaction between warmup heuristics and kernel selector.
marco: throwing a profiling snippet for one affected request (kernel selection trace):
```
[01:12:23.421] kernel_selector: evaluate candidates 3
[01:12:23.422] kernel_selector: prefer fast_attn_v2 (cost=12.1)
[01:12:23.435] batching: waited 38ms (window>threshold) -> dispatched
[01:12:23.456] runtime: kv_cache_miss: 0.28 -> eviction_rate spike
[01:12:23.467] response_latency: 152ms
```
meera: kv cache miss rate up — warmup scheduler holding requests longer probably increases seq lengths in batches and pollutes hotset causing more evictions.
devon: can we reproduce locally? I can run the nightly sample harness with the new batch defaults + kernel prober enabled.
nina: please do. In parallel: rollback candidate = revert commit `a1b2c3` from #4029 (revert change to default batch hold) to see if it drops back.
aj: running bisect now across canary replica groups to narrow host/commit. quick grep shows a subtle change in `scheduler::should_warmup()` that delays kernel prober early exits.
marco: added a flamegraph link (internal): https://perf.redwood.local/flame/5381234567 — main hot path is scheduler spin + kernel probe, adds ~18ms per request at p95.
meera: if warmup probes are running in-band they can shift batching timing; older scheduler probed asynchronously. PR moved probes to inline fast path for startup correctness.
devon: local run started — baseline workload (mix A) with new defaults. reproducing: p95 ~150ms vs baseline 95ms. KV eviction rate doubled in 30s.
aj: OK revert queued in release manager (deploy-revert #5381234). canary rollback in ~10m if CI green.
meera: if revert fixes it, we need a follow-up that moves probes back async but with stronger correctness checks. create follow-up ticket.
perf-bot: bisect summary: suspect range commits 4024..4032, highest delta mapped to 4029.
ci-bot: perf-job-5381234700: smoke tests passed, but end-to-end perf suite pending.
nina: plan: 1) pause rollout to more clusters, 2) apply immediate revert to canary, 3) run full perf harness, 4) create action item to redesign warmup async probe. assigned to aj/meera/devon.
marco: +1. leaving traces and logs in #artifacts/5381234567.
aj: quick note — if revert doesn't restore p95, we'll inspect kernel selection heuristic thresholds (cost model). but current signal strongly points to batching/warmup interaction.
devon: reproducer and logs in my branch `perf/repro-warmup-batch`. sharing steps in thread artifacts.
nina: thanks all. I'm going to watch the rollback and update this thread when canary metrics show recovery. :thumbsup:
